en: I meditate on Hari, who is known through the Garbha Upanishad, who wakes the child in the womb to its own Self, and who is found when the body is set aside: Hari, who is nothing but my own Self.
Om. May He protect us both, teacher and student. May He nourish us both. May we work together with strength. May our study be full of light. May we never quarrel. Om, peace, peace, peace.

first: ॐ पञ्चात्मकं पञ्चसु वर्तमानं षडाश्रयं षड्गुणयोगयुक्तम् ।
en: Om. The body is made of five, lives among five, rests on six supports and is joined with six qualities. It has seven tissues and three impurities, two sources of birth, and is made of four kinds of food. Why is it called “made of five”? Because of earth, water, fire, air and space. In this body of five, what is earth, what is water, what is fire, what is air and what is space? What is hard in it is earth, what is liquid is water, what is hot is fire, what moves is air, and what is hollow is called space. Earth holds the body up, water binds it into a whole, fire gives light, air moves it, and space gives it room. Each sense has its own work: the ear hears sound, the skin feels touch, the eyes see form, the tongue tastes and the nose smells. Why “six supports”? Because it knows the six tastes: sweet, sour, salty, bitter, pungent and astringent. And there are the seven notes of music: shadja, rishabha, gandhara, madhyama, panchama, dhaivata and nishada. Pleasant and unpleasant sounds, by attention, become of ten kinds.

first: शुक्लो रक्तः कृष्णो धूम्रः पीतः कपिलः पाण्डुर इति ।
en: White, red, dark, smoky, yellow, tawny and pale: these are the seven colours. Why “of seven tissues”? When food and other things reach a person, then, because their qualities suit one another, the six-fold essence (rasa) arises. From the essence comes blood; from blood, flesh; from flesh, fat; from fat, sinews; from sinews, bones; from bones, marrow; and from marrow, seed. From the union of seed and blood the embryo forms, and it is settled in the heart. In the heart is the inner fire; in the place of fire is bile; in the place of bile is air; and in the place of air is the heart, in the order set by Prajapati.

first: ऋतुकाले सम्प्रयोगादेकरात्रोषितं कलिलं भवति सप्तरात्रोषितं बुद्बुदं भवति अर्धमासाभ्यन्तरेण पिण्डो भवति ।
en: From union in the right season, after one night it is a soft mass; after seven nights, a bubble; within half a month, a lump; and within a month it becomes firm. In two months the head forms; in three months the feet. In the fourth month the ankles, belly and hips form; in the fifth, the spine; in the sixth, the mouth, nose, eyes and ears. In the seventh month it is joined with the living soul (jiva), and in the eighth it is complete in every feature. When the father's seed is stronger, a boy is born; when the mother's is stronger, a girl; when both are equal, a child of neither sex. When the parents' minds are troubled, children are born blind, lame, hunchbacked or very short. When the seed is split in two, pressed by the airs of both parents, the body becomes two, and twins are born. Made of five and now able, with an intellect of five parts that knows smell, taste and the rest, it thinks on the imperishable syllable Om. Knowing this one syllable, the eight elements of nature and the sixteen changes take shape in the body of that embodied one. Then its breath is fed through the cord that carries what the mother eats and drinks. In the ninth month it is complete with every feature, with knowledge and with its senses. It remembers its earlier births and knows its good and bad deeds.

(The child thinks:) “I have seen thousands of earlier wombs. I have eaten many kinds of food and drunk from many breasts. I have been born and have died, born again and again. For the good and bad deeds I did for my family, I burn here alone, while those who enjoyed their fruits are gone. Alas, I am sunk in an ocean of sorrow and see no way out. If I am freed from the womb, I will take refuge in Maheshvara, who destroys evil and gives the fruit of liberation. If I am freed from the womb, I will take refuge in Narayana, who destroys evil and gives the fruit of liberation. If I am freed from the womb, I will meditate on the eternal Brahman.” Then, reaching the door of the womb and squeezed as if in a press, it is born in great pain. As soon as it is born, the Vaishnava air of the world touches it, and then it no longer remembers its births and deaths, nor knows its good and bad deeds.

Why is it called sharira, the body? Because fires dwell (shriyante) in it: the fire of knowledge, the fire of sight and the fire of the belly. The fire of the belly digests what is eaten, drunk, licked and sucked. The fire of sight lets us see forms and the rest. The fire of knowledge knows good and bad deeds. These fires have three places: the Ahavaniya fire in the mouth, the Garhapatya in the belly and the Dakshina fire in the heart. In this sacrifice the Self is the one who offers it, the mind is the priest, greed and the other faults are the animals offered, steadiness and contentment are the vow, the senses of knowing are the sacred vessels, and the organs of action are the offerings. The head is the bowl, the hair is the sacred grass, and the mouth is the inner altar. The head has four skull plates. There are sixteen rows of side teeth and lips, a hundred and seven vital points, a hundred and eighty joints, a hundred and nine sinews, seven hundred veins, five hundred measures of marrow, three hundred and sixty bones and three and a half crore hairs. The heart weighs eight palas and the tongue twelve. There is one prastha of bile, one adhaka of phlegm, one kudava of seed and two prasthas of fat; urine and faeces vary with the food eaten. This is the teaching on liberation of Pippalada; the teaching on liberation of Pippalada is complete.
Om. May He protect us both, teacher and student. May He nourish us both. May we work together with strength. May our study be full of light. May we never quarrel. Om, peace, peace, peace.
